title: Stress spikes precede spontaneous late remodelling in the simulated tissue

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stress spikes precede spontaneous late remodelling in the simulated tissue

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, the tissue spontaneously remodels long after its pattern has stabilized, without external perturbation, and a sharp spike in stress immediately precedes each onset of morphogenetic activity, suggesting that stress drives the morphogenetic changes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue maintains allostasis in adulthood

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In our simulations, a dramatic spike in stress immediately precedes the sharp onset of extensive morphogenetic activity (see electronic supplementary material, figure S1a), suggesting that stress drives the morphogenetic changes in the tissue.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › The tissue maintains allostasis in adulthood”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.87

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The public model permits both replication of the time ordering and direct in-silico intervention, giving stronger discrimination than the reported correlation alone. Coverage across evolved tissues remains a limitation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run long unperturbed trajectories, detect stress spikes and remodeling onsets using prespecified thresholds, and intervene by clamping or shifting stress before predicted events. Temporal precedence is confirmed observationally; prevention or delay tests whether stress drives remodeling in the model.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Temporal precedence alone does not establish causation.

The reported pattern may be controller-specific.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stress and morphogenetic activity are both variables in the public model, so lead-lag can be recomputed on long runs. The published observation is one tissue's trace, and the causal wording goes beyond precedence. Re-simulation can check whether spikes lead remodelling in this system, not that stress is the driver in general.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run an unperturbed evolved tissue past pattern stabilization and test whether each burst of cell-state change is immediately preceded by a spike in the model's stress variable. Spikes leading every remodelling onset would support the temporal claim; remodelling without a prior spike, or spikes that do not lead activity, would refute it. Precedence still would not prove that stress drives the change.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The result is reported for a representative individual, not as a pre-registered rate across tissues.

A spike before movement is compatible with a common cause inside the network.
